title: Laboratory run-event stream (design proposal, unreleased)
description: Draft schema for Roadmap 0.2. A run-event stream records what a laboratory run issued, what the hardware acknowledged, what was physically observed, what a human did, and where the material ended up, as an ordered sequence of typed events rather than as prose reconstructed afterwards. The event types are one-to-one with the ten Observability Coverage fields in data/metrics/b5_observability.csv, and the failure fields are the ones data/metrics/b6_preflight_preventability.csv had to code by hand. This is a proposal: no published metric reads from it, and it is not a standard.

schema_version.description: Pinned so an early consumer cannot mistake a proposal for a stable contract.

run_id.description: Immutable identifier for one execution of one method. Every event in the stream belongs to this run.

method_identity.description: Version-bound identity of the executed method, ideally a content digest. null when the emitting system cannot bind one, which is itself the finding rather than a formatting problem.

notes.description: Free text about the stream as a whole. Never a substitute for an event.

events.description: Ordered events. `sequence` must be strictly increasing; ordering is carried explicitly because wall-clock timestamps from a scheduler and a device are not reliably comparable.

event_id.description: Unique within the stream. Referenced by `acknowledges` and `restores`.

sequence.description: Strictly increasing position in the run.

recorded_at.description: Emitter clock time. Optional and explicitly nullable: an event whose time is unknown must still be recordable in order, because dropping it is worse than admitting the gap.

event_type.description: One of thirteen types covering the ten Observability Coverage fields. The mapping is tabulated in docs/event-schema.md.

actor.description: Which participant emitted the event. A modeled state change asserted by a scheduler and a physical observation reported by a device are different kinds of evidence and must not be merged.

command.description: The operation requested, at the granularity the control system dispatches.

physically_irreversible.description: Whether completing this command changes material or hardware state in a way no later software action undoes. This single flag is what makes the completed irreversible prefix computable after an abort, which is the reconstruction data/metrics/b6_preflight_preventability.csv had to perform by reading a thread.

preflight_checkable.description: Whether the preconditions of this command were fully knowable before dispatch. null when the emitter cannot determine it; null is not false.

acknowledges.description: The `event_id` of the command this event acknowledges.

outcome.description: What became of the acknowledged command. `unknown` is available on purpose: three of the four coded observability cases scored zero on acknowledgment, and an honest unknown is the finding.

observation.description: What was physically sensed or seen, stated as the measurement rather than as its interpretation.

modeled_state.description: The control system's own belief about state after this event. Recorded separately from `observation` so a divergence between model and reality is visible instead of averaged away.

severity.description: Severity of a warning or failure event.

message.description: Emitter-supplied text for a warning or failure.

failure_class.description: Coarse failure kind, using the classes already coded in data/metrics/b6_preflight_preventability.csv.

preflight_detectable.description: Whether this failure was knowable before the run began. `indeterminate` is a required member of the vocabulary, not a convenience: one of the four coded preflight scenarios is genuinely indeterminate, and a two-valued field would have forced it to a wrong answer.

intervention.description: What a human physically or logically did. Recorded as an event rather than inferred from a gap in the log.

recovery.description: The action taken to return the system or the material to a defined state.

restores.description: The `event_id`s of the irreversible commands this recovery addresses. Empty means the recovery addressed none of them, which is a claim the stream should have to make explicitly.

material_disposition.description: Where the material actually ended up. The weakest field in the coded corpus: no case fully recorded it, and `unknown` must remain expressible so a stream cannot imply an accounting it does not have.

disposition_evidence.description: What independently supports the stated disposition, for example a mass or volume measurement. null when the disposition is asserted by the control system alone.
